title: Book 6 — Erato, Chapter 106
paragraphs: On this occasion, however — the time when he said Pan had appeared to him — Pheidippides, having been sent by the generals, was in Sparta the day after he left Athens. When he came before the magistrates he said: “Men of Lacedaemon, the Athenians beg you to come to their aid and not to allow a city most anciently established among the Greeks to fall into slavery at the hands of barbarians. Eretria has already been enslaved, and Greece has been made the weaker by the loss of a famous city.” He delivered the message with which he had been charged, and they were willing enough to help the Athenians, but it was not possible for them to move at once, since they did not wish to break their law. It was the ninth day of the month, and on the ninth day, they said, they would not march out, nor before the moon was full.
